record: Sprint 06 fixture / metric / acceptance-limit freeze (execution order step 3) — recorded before any VAL-019..022 result was evaluated

metrics.alignment: declared integer latency only (native and reference report the same value; verified); no fitted gain/DC/clock/delay
metrics.comparison_point: native output before output trim (trim 0 dB in every fixture; trim law tested separately) vs reference cascade output
metrics.rms_limit: RMS(error) <= max(1e-5 * RMS(input), 1e-7) per channel, RMS(input) over the fixture frames
metrics.per_fixture: each (fixture, rate, state, channel) cell PASS/FAIL individually; never averaged
metrics.discrete_rules: SP 12-bit codes, MPC 18-bit codes and 16-bit codes compared exactly per machine sample (native taps vs reference taps); any difference reported with index, native/reference code, the sampler value and the output consequence
metrics.determinism: two native renders bit-identical (sha256 of the output bytes); block partitions (64 / irregular / seeded / single-call) bit-identical

acceptance_limits_owner_set.discrete: exact code agreement; discrepancies reported, never waived

cross_rate_method_frozen.stimuli: fixtures multitone_mix_m12, transient_bursts, sine_1k_m20 (common band < 18 kHz, continuous-time origin t=0)
cross_rate_method_frozen.analysis_conversion: Kaiser-windowed sinc resampler (smlsp3000.nullframework.kaiser_sinc_interpolate; half_width 64, beta 12) from each host rate to the 44.1 kHz analysis grid followed by an analysis low-pass at 18 kHz (FFT brick wall on the 44.1 kHz grid), both characterised separately on the analytic stimulus itself (tool error = |conv(x_rate) - x_44.1k| in the same metric)
cross_rate_method_frozen.alignment: each render aligned by its own declared latency; physical time origin shared (t = 0 at input sample 0)
cross_rate_method_frozen.comparison: d_ref(rate) = RMS(conv(ref_rate) - ref_44.1k); d_nat(rate) = RMS(conv(nat_rate) - nat_44.1k); requirement: production meets the same-rate budget at every rate first; then |d_nat - d_ref| <= G * e_rate + e_44.1k + tool_error where e_rate is the measured same-rate native-vs-reference RMS error at that rate and G the resampler's measured gain bound (<= 1.001)
cross_rate_method_frozen.note: the quantizer-boundary dependence of the reference's own cross-rate behaviour is reported as is (frozen policy), not claimed as an absolute cross-rate identity

convergence_method_frozen.stimuli: sine_1k_m20, near_nyquist_tone_19k, multitone_mix_m12, overrange_steps_pm16 (stepped clamp), two-tone 18 kHz + 19.5 kHz
convergence_method_frozen.alignment: each render by its own declared integer latency (latency may differ by the D15 rounding between proxy ratios); same physical origin
convergence_method_frozen.metric: RMS and spectral-line differences 8x vs 16x of the REFERENCE itself (model self-convergence), and native-vs-reference at both ratios; categories: SP images/fold-back (intentional, documented), converter-clamp harmonics (intentional), implementation filtering error (8x vs 16x), production-introduced difference (native vs reference at the same ratio)

method_correction_before_final_run.what: cross-rate analysis conversion: the 18 kHz brick-wall low-pass is applied on the SOURCE-rate grid BEFORE the Kaiser-sinc evaluation on the 44.1 kHz grid (the first implementation filtered after the interpolation, so SP images/fold-back products between 22.05 kHz and the source Nyquist aliased into the band and inflated the reference's own cross-rate discrepancy to about −7 dB re signal on the multitone fixture, while the 1 kHz tone showed −51 dB)
method_correction_before_final_run.why_it_is_not_a_tolerance_change: the bound formula, the fixtures, the metric and the limits are unchanged; only the analysis tool's filter order was corrected to do what the frozen description says (compare the common band); the first run's outcome was already PASS
method_correction_before_final_run.recorded: before the final VAL-019 record was produced (the first record is superseded, not kept as evidence)
